chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Abū Ismāʿīl al-Sarrāj, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said:
I saw Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while he was in sajdah, and he had raised his feet from the ground, with one of his feet upon the other.
So the proper interpretation of this report is that it is possible that he عليه السلام only did that due to a necessity that compelled him to it, not in a state of choice.

key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the ground, from which the feet were raised
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith being discussed
key_terms.الْوَجْهُ: the correct interpretive approach or explanation of the report
key_terms.حَالِ الِاخْتِيَارِ: the state of voluntary choice, as opposed to compulsion or necessity
key_terms.قَدَمَيْهِ: his two feet, relevant here to the posture of sajdah
key_terms.لِضَرُورَةٍ: due to necessity, indicating an exceptional circumstance

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith scholars understand a report of the Imam عليه السلام raising his feet during sajdah?
ai.summary: This report describes Imām al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام being seen in sajdah with his feet raised from the ground and one foot over the other. The text then explains that this action should be understood as having occurred due to necessity, not as the normal rule in a voluntary state, indicating a jurisprudential distinction in the rulings of sajdah.
